work.text: A configuration file: the parameter settings for one of the supported variant callers, the software that decides which differences in a sequenced genome are real mutations. The miner never runs the genome itself. What is paid for is the recipe that, when the validator runs it on this round's synthetic genome, finds the planted mutations best.

scoring.text: Validators run each configuration in a Docker container on the round's genome and compare the calls to the planted truth with hap.py, a standard genomics referee. Under v2, live per the network config: score = 100 x (0.70 x core + 0.30 x germline). Core is F1 per variant class by fixed difficulty weights, one-base indels heaviest at 0.40; germline penalizes false positives; a plausibility gate zeroes an implausible callset.
scoring.quote: V2_CORE_WEIGHT = 0.70; V2_GERMLINE_WEIGHT = 0.30

split.text: Winner-heavy. The top eligible miner of the round gets 0.8 of the weight; ranks 2 to 20 split the remaining 0.2 in slices that shrink by 0.9 each rank; everyone else gets nothing. A miner is eligible only after scoring in 5 of the last 20 finalized rounds. Validators fetch these values live; the code's defaults are fallbacks.

split.disagrees: The about page and whitepaper say the top miner wins 100 percent of emissions (sn107-004, Winner-Take-All); the code's fallback defaults are 0.9 winner and 0.8 decay (utils/weight_tracking.py); the live config on 2026-09-19 is 0.8 and 0.9.

work.text: GPU time by the second. A miner, called a provider, runs a small coordinator plus one or more NVIDIA GPU machines and sets an hourly price per machine. What is paid for is a machine that passes the validator's probe: rented machines are paid from one pool, eligible idle machines of the listed models from another.

scoring.text: Two formulas. A rented machine scores score x gpu_portion x gpu_count / total count of that model, where gpu_portion is a per-model share the platform derives from rental revenue. An idle machine of an eligible model scores gpu_count x hourly_rate x a cap multiplier, min(idle GPUs in its tier, tier cap) / idle GPUs. Both are multiplied by sysbox, driver and uptime gates.
scoring.quote: result.rental_share * result.gpu_count * result.effective_rate / result.total_rental_cost

split.text: Three pools, each proportional inside. Rented machines share the mining pool by score. Idle eligible machines share a second pool sized by their dollar rate per epoch divided by 0.41 and by the epoch's emission in dollars, capped at the burn ceiling. What the idle pool does not claim goes to designated burn UIDs. The packaged ceiling is 0.91, so the rented pool is 0.09.

A forfeit scores -12. The challenger crowns if its mean margin clears max(2 standard errors, 0.2 sd), the thought floor and causality gate.

work.text: A hosted computer-vision model. The miner trains a model for one or more Elements (named tasks such as detecting players in football footage), deploys it on Chutes, a separate Bittensor subnet that rents model hosting, and records its fingerprint on chain. scoring.text: Per Element, each answer is scored on pillars (for example overlap with the answer key, player count, smoothness, role), each pillar times its manifest weight, summed. The sum is gated: subtract the Element's baseline theta, floor at delta_floor, multiply by beta, a difficulty factor. The answer key is real ground truth or a SAM3 segmentation. The winner is the highest average over at least 30 challenges in a 3-day window.
scoring.quote: return max(self.apply_baseline_gate(score=score), self.delta_floor); return self.beta * improvement

work.text: A trading record. A miner is an account on Hyperliquid, a perpetuals exchange, trading its own money. On each overlap a utility U rewards compounded return and absolute profit and penalizes drawdown, downside volatility and profit concentrated in few days; G = (e^(1.5U) - 1)/(e^1.5 - 1), halved if trailing-30-day PnL is negative or recent volume is thin. The winner banks the margin; margins sum to the score.

work.text: A clique: a set of vertices in a validator-supplied graph in which every pair is connected, returned inside a time limit of 6 to 30 seconds. Graphs are general, 290 to 900 vertices in the code. Problems come from the validators' own database, each served at most once across all validators; no outside party supplies a graph.

scoring.text: Validity first: an invalid or non-maximal clique scores zero. Optimality is exp of minus the share of miners with a larger clique divided by the miner's size relative to the round's largest, normalised to the round's best. Diversity is one over the count of miners returning the identical vertex set, normalised. The final score is optimality times one plus difficulty, plus diversity.

scoring.disagrees: docs/mechanism.md gives three problem classes at difficulty 0.2, 0.4 and 1; CliqueAI/selection/problem_selector.py at the same commit ships four classes at 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 and 1.0, the fourth at 890 to 900 vertices.

split.text: Top-heavy, not proportional. Per-problem scores fold into a debiased exponential moving average with alpha 0.01, a half-life of about 69 samples. At weight time the averages are min-max normalised, passed through a sigmoid centred on the median with the interquartile range as steepness, then raised to a power chosen so the top half of miners takes 80 percent of the weight.

work.text: A media-provenance classifier: a model that takes an image, video or audio clip and returns class scores for real against synthetic. scoring.text: Per modality a detector is benchmarked on public, private holdout and generator-made samples and scored by sn34_score, which combines classification performance, the Matthews correlation coefficient, with probability calibration, the Brier score, under round-specific sample weights. work.text: Answered JSON-RPC requests. What is paid for is compute units served at the bid price, checked for correctness afterwards.

scoring.text: Work times price. Each epoch the validator reads the gateway's manifest of compute units each miner served, multiplies non-archive and archive units by that miner's own bid prices in dollars, and that dollar figure is the score. Quality is not in the formula; it acts earlier, in the routing score and burst tests that decide how much traffic a node gets. Correctness is checked afterwards against reference nodes.

split.text: Proportional to dollars consumed. Each miner's weight is its consumed USD over the total. The miner pool is 41 percent of epoch emission. The scale between pool and consumption is unclamped both ways, so the pool is filled exactly and nothing burns, unless the scale exceeds 10: then consumption is paid at face value and the rest goes to burn sink UID 103. Banned coldkeys get zero.
